said:
On Nacre walking remains the baseline
The ten starting locations are accessible on foot through the previously established connections. Vehicles offer convenience, cargo capacity and protection from the weather. They are not required to complete the first assignment.
There are no antigravity hover vehicles. Local transport uses wheels, tracks or conventional propulsion.
Scheduled transport services
| Transport | Route and stops | Departure | Journey time | Cost |
| Ridge Crawler | Arrival Lock → Workshop → Ridge Shelter → Orison Listening Room | Workdays at 07:30 from Arrival Lock; return at 17:00 from Orison. No scheduled service on Restday. | 20 minutes for the whole route, including short stops. | 3 credits per single journey. Official travel for the investigation is paid from the research budget. |
| Coast Runner | Port Vesper → Kestrel Landing, a more distant supply post on Nacre | Primeday and Anchor at 09:00; return at 15:00. Board through Arrival Lock. | 90 minutes each way, weather permitting. | 25 credits per single journey. |
| Belt Tender | Nacre orbit ↔ the wider Lantern Belt transport network | No daily service. Arrivals are listed in advance in the port register; delays occur. | Interplanetary journeys take days to weeks; interstellar journeys much longer. | By contract. The player's inbound journey is already paid for. |

The Ridge Crawler is an enclosed electric tracked vehicle for people and materials. A driver from the support team operates the scheduled service. It uses a maintenance track beside the walking route; these are not additional accessible locations.
The Coast Runner is a small crewed electric aircraft operating on the same planet. It is not a spacecraft. During the first phase, Kestrel Landing remains a distant destination, not yet a fully developed play area.
Delays and missed services
Mara manages bookings and departure notices. The driver or pilot decides whether a journey can depart safely.
If the player misses the Crawler, they can walk, wait or request transport.
A cancelled flight is refunded or rebooked.
A booked journey genuinely reserves a seat; the vehicle does not have unlimited capacity.
A weather forecast is a forecast. A departure is only definitively cancelled on the basis of conditions or an authorised decision.
Before departure, the player sees the destination, expected duration, price and known restrictions.
Hiring transport
Through Mara, with technical handover by Tessa, the player can hire a Trail Cart: a small electric four-wheeled vehicle with two seats and a cargo rack.
| Condition | Agreement |
| Price | 12 credits for eight hours. |
| Deposit | 30 credits, returned if the vehicle is handed back undamaged. |
| Range | Enough for two return journeys between Port Vesper and Orison under normal conditions. |
| Route | Maintenance track only; no stairs, loose rocky slopes or vulnerable coastal beds. |
| Journey time | About 25 minutes from Arrival Lock to Orison, including careful driving on the climb. |
| Requirement | A brief driving and safety instruction. |
| Return | To Workshop, no later than the agreed time. |

The Trail Cart has a windscreen and rain canopy, but does not protect against all winter conditions. A hire contract records the driver, vehicle, cargo, initial condition and return time.
If the assignment requires the vehicle, the research budget may cover the hire and deposit. This must be agreed in advance. Damage or late return has consequences based on what actually happened; a route closed by the port does not automatically constitute negligence.
The Peregrine
The Peregrine is not a scheduled service and cannot be hired. Departure becomes possible only when:
the first signal investigation is complete;
the crew and roles are established;
technical readiness, medical preparation and supplies have been approved;
the player has accepted the expedition contract.
There are at most six places, including the player. The research budget pays for the ship; the player does not buy a personal ticket to Echo Nine.
In conventional flight, the Peregrine travels below light speed. The experimental drive is a separate, prepared manoeuvre with established conditions, risks and consequences. It must not become unrestricted fast travel to every named place.
Distant destinations
| Destination | Significance | Availability |
| Kestrel Landing | Another settlement on Nacre, with a larger warehouse and parts trade. | To be developed later; suitable for a short supply mission. |
| Meridian Anchorage | A small transfer station in orbit around Nacre. Larger transport ships dock here. | Accessible later by a booked conventional shuttle. |
| Harrow Station | The player's place of origin, elsewhere in the Lantern Belt. | Far away; no short return trip during the first investigation. |
| Echo Nine | Provisional designation for the destination emerging from the signal investigation. | Accessible only once the experimental expedition actually departs. |

The names of distant places may already be known without being immediately playable. The journal must clearly indicate whether a route is known, available or still uncertain.
What may happen along the way
Events follow from the terrain, weather and whoever is actually travelling. Not every journey needs an incident.
| Along the way | Possible event | Player's choice |
| Coastal Service Path | Fog hides the next route marker. | Proceed more slowly, trust navigation or return to the shelter. |
| Near Ridge Shelter | A maintenance team is trying to repair a faulty relay cabinet. | Help, ask for information or continue walking. |
| On the climb to Orison | A storm has scattered loose material across the track. | Clear a safe passage, wait or continue on foot if possible. |
| In the Ridge Crawler | A fellow traveller shares news from personal experience. | Ask more, make an appointment or let the conversation rest. |
| During a longer flight | Weather forces a delay or a different landing. | Discuss waiting, rebooking or an alternative destination. |

A navigation error usually costs time or takes the player to a recognisable wrong point. A short walk must not become endless through successive unlucky checks.
For the Chronicler
Let journey time genuinely pass: people continue working, shops close and appointments approach. Interrupt a journey when the player must make a meaningful decision; summarise quiet stretches.
Transport also moves goods and information. A delayed flight may hold up a part. A traveller may bring news, but knows only what they saw or heard personally.
The first journey to Orison should make distance tangible. Later journeys may become familiar and efficient — until something really changes.
